children: Alibaba (BABA) warned U.S. curbs on Nvidia chips may slow cloud revenue growth to 30%–45% in 2027, from 53% last quarter. CEO Eddie Wu sees growth reaching 50% or more in 2028.
Alibaba ADR (BABA) fell 1.26% to $83.31 on Nov. 19 after reporting September-quarter revenue up 10% year over year to RMB271.5 billion. AI cloud and compute revenue rose 53% to RMB61 billion.
Citigroup kept its Buy rating on Alibaba (BABA) but cut its target to $160 from $193, citing sector valuation declines. Barclays lowered its target to $155 from $200; Baird cut to $128 from $160.
Alibaba (BABA) plans to sharply expand production of its in-house T-Head AI chips by 2027. The company says the processors can now train and run AI models.
Alibaba (BABA) shareholders filed a proposed class-action suit in Manhattan, alleging its 2024–2026 annual reports understated risks tied to Singapore-based Megaspeed and U.S. export controls.
Alibaba executive Wu said computing capacity remains supply-constrained, while domestic capacity is set to drive cloud revenue growth.
Mizuho maintained its Outperform rating on Alibaba Group Holding Limited Sponsored ADR (BABA) and raised its price target to $205 from $200.
